introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2020. Duration: two and a half hours. Do ALL the tasks (Task 1, Task 2 and Task 3) specified in the question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three. Each version has three tasks: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task 3 (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the pictures 'foxandstork' and 'hareandtortoise' found on the desktop) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP ONE - TASK 1 (20 marks)**

*Figure 1 shows a story typed and enclosed in a frame. Your task is to type, edit and format the text as requested.*

> **The Cunning Fox and the Clever Stork** *(title in bold, centred and underlined)*
>
> Once upon a time, there lived a very cunning and mischievous fox. He used to speak to other animals sweetly and gain their trust, before playing tricks on them. One day the fox met a stork. He befriended the stork and acted like a very good friend. Soon, he invited the stork to have a feast with him. The stork happily accepted the invitation.
>
> The day of the feast came, and the stork went to the fox's house. To her surprise and disappointment, the fox said that he could not make a big feast as promised, and just offered some soup. When he brought the soup out of the kitchen, the stork saw that it was in a shallow bowl! The poor stork could not have any soup with its long bill, but the fox easily licked the soup from the plate...
>
> The day arrived and the fox reached the stork's place. After exchanging pleasantries, the stork served soup for both of them, in a narrow jar with a long neck. She was able to have the soup very easily with her long bill, but the fox obviously could not. After finishing hers, the stork asked the fox if he was enjoying the soup. The fox remembered the feast he himself had given the stork, and felt very ashamed. He stammered, "I...I'd better leave now. I have a tummy ache." Humiliated, he left the place running.
>
> *Morale: One bad turn begets another.*
>
> Source https://www.kidsworldfun.com/shortstories_foxandstork.php
>
> **Figure 1**

questions.enonce_markdown: State the name(s) of the word processor(s) installed in your PC.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The answer depends on the software installed on the candidate's PC, so give the real name(s) found on that machine, for example **Microsoft Word** (or **LibreOffice Writer**, **WPS Writer**). Check it in the *Start* menu or in the *File* > *Account* / *About* window of the program you use. A correct answer names at least one real word processor, not a spreadsheet or a browser.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch a word processor program from your PC and type the text of Figure 1. Justify the three paragraphs.  *[10 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Typing.** Start the word processor (for example *Start* > *Microsoft Word* > *Blank document*) and type the text of Figure 1 exactly as printed: the title, the three paragraphs (press *Enter* only at the end of each paragraph, never at the end of a line, and let the program wrap the lines), the line *Morale: One bad turn begets another.* and the line *Source https://www.kidsworldfun.com/shortstories_foxandstork.php*. Keep the spelling, the capital letters, the punctuation (the exclamation mark in paragraph 2, the three dots at the end of paragraph 2, the quotation marks in paragraph 3) and the indentation of the first line of each paragraph (use the *Tab* key or the first-line indent).

**Justifying.** Select the three paragraphs (click at the beginning of the first one, hold *Shift* and click at the end of the third) and click the **Justify** button in the *Home* tab, *Paragraph* group (shortcut *Ctrl + J*). Both the left and the right edges of each paragraph are now straight.

*Marking idea:* most of the 10 marks reward the complete and accurate typing of the text; the rest reward the justified paragraphs (the split is indicative, the Board's mark scheme is not known).

questions.enonce_markdown: For the title, Bold, Center, underline, and apply a font size of 16.  *[1 mark]*
Add a light blue background colour to the title.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: With the title still selected, open the drop-down arrow of the **Shading** button (paint bucket) in the *Home* tab, *Paragraph* group, and choose a light blue from the palette (for example *Blue, Accent 1, Lighter 80%*, or *More Colors...* and a pale blue). The colour fills the background behind the title. Do not confuse it with the *Font Color* button (the colour of the letters).

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the body text and apply a serif font of size 12.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the body text, that is the three paragraphs of the story (click before the first word of paragraph 1, then *Shift* + click after the last word of paragraph 3). In the *Home* tab, open the font box and choose a **serif** font (a font whose letters have small strokes at their ends), for example **Times New Roman** (or Cambria, Georgia, Book Antiqua). Then open the size box and choose **12**.

A sans-serif font such as Arial or Calibri would lose the mark for the font.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert the image called 'foxandstork' (found on the desktop) at the left of the first paragraph and wrap text to its right.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Click at the beginning of the first paragraph (*Once upon a time ...*).
2. *Insert* tab > **Pictures** > *This Device* (or *Picture from file*), open the **Desktop**, select **foxandstork** and click *Insert*.
3. Select the picture, click the **Layout Options** icon next to it (or *Picture Format* > *Wrap Text*) and choose **Square** (or *Tight*). Text now flows around the picture.
4. Drag the picture to the left side of the first paragraph (or *Picture Format* > *Position* > *Position in Middle Left with Square Text Wrapping*) and resize it with a corner handle if it is too big.

The picture is on the left of the first paragraph and the text of that paragraph is wrapped to its right. *[The picture file is supplied on the day; it is not in the printed paper.]*

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert page number as header.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: *Insert* tab > **Page Number** > **Top of Page** > choose a style (for example *Plain Number 1*, *2* or *3*). The page number is placed in the header area, at the top of every page. (Another way: double-click in the top margin to open the header, then *Insert* > *Page Number* > *Current Position*, or *Insert* > *Quick Parts* > *Field* > *Page*.) Close the header with *Close Header and Footer*. The number must be in the header, not in the footer.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert a footer with the text 'One bad turn begets another' at the bottom left.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: *Insert* tab > **Footer** > **Edit Footer** (or *Blank*). Type **One bad turn begets another** in the footer, make sure the paragraph is **left aligned** (*Home* > *Align Left*, *Ctrl + L*), then click *Close Header and Footer*. The text appears at the bottom left of every page.

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task 1 in your working directory.
questions.corrige_markdown: *File* > **Save As** > *Browse*, open the working directory (the folder named by the supervisor), type the file name **Task 1** and click *Save*.
*File* > **Print** (*Ctrl + P*), check the printer and the number of copies (1), then click *Print*. Collect the printed copy and attach it to the booklet.
